expectations.text: States the SME exemption: small and micro enterprises may opt out of specified obligations (impact assessments, certain security/processor duties) for 5 years from January 1, 2026
expectations.evidence: "Article 38, together with Decree 356, gives small and micro enterprises a five-year opt-out (from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2030)" from "Article 21 — mandatory domestic DPIA... Article 22 — certain security measures... Article 33(2) — certain processor-specific obligations"

expectations.text: Notes the carve-outs: the exemption does NOT apply if processing sensitive personal data or processing at large scale
expectations.evidence: "unless they process sensitive personal data or process at large scale"; "The exemption evaporates the moment you process sensitive personal data... or process 'at large scale'"

expectations.text: Notes micro-enterprises get the fullest relief, subject to the same carve-outs
expectations.evidence: "Micro-enterprises are fully exempt from these unless they process sensitive personal data or process at large scale"

expectations.text: Warns that core duties still apply: lawful basis/consent, data subject rights, breach notification, and the penalty regime (Decree 330) applies to violations of applicable duties
expectations.evidence: "Do not defer consent mechanics, rights-fulfilment processes, or breach response planning... Decree 330/2026/ND-CP's penalty framework (effective August 2026) applies the same fines to small companies"

expectations.text: Advises documenting the exemption reliance and re-checking on growth/scale changes
expectations.evidence: "document the basis for claiming the exemption"; "expect to cross the 'large scale' threshold as you grow, plan for DPIA compliance now"
